purpose: Minocycline is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as acne, certain skin infections, urinary tract infections, and some sexually transmitted infections. It can also be used for respiratory tract infections and conditions like rosacea. Your doctor may prescribe it for other infections caused by certain types of bacteria.
how_it_works: Minocycline works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Think of it like cutting off the bacteria's food supply so they can no longer thrive. Over time, the bacteria die off and your body's immune system can clear the infection.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, or upset stomach are common, especially if taken on an empty stomach. You may also notice dizziness, lightheadedness, or a spinning feeling. Some people get headaches, skin sensitivity to sunlight, or discoloration of the skin, teeth, or gums with long-term use.
warnings: Do not take minocycline if you are pregnant, as it can harm the developing baby's bones and teeth. Avoid taking it with dairy products, antacids, or iron supplements, as these can reduce how well the medication works. Contact your doctor right away if you develop severe headaches, blurred vision, chest pain, difficulty swallowing, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash or swelling. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so use sunscreen and protective clothing outdoors.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg twice daily, or sometimes 50 mg to 100 mg once or twice a day depending on what it is being treated. For acne, a lower dose extended-release tablet is often taken once daily. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed and finish the full course even if you feel better.
